items.transcript:
Good morning. This is Briefly Daily for Tuesday, the 8th of September. Here are today's most important stories, across World, Business. Everything you hear is assembled from the sources named alongside it. Where reporting is contested, we say so rather than picking a side.

Story 1. World. Cyclone Verath makes landfall near Kalpore, 40,000 evacuated. Wind speeds reached 110 kmph, the state disaster authority said, 40,000 evacuated as Cyclone Verath, on Friday; power supply was disrupted in coastal areas. Hindustan Times, NDTV, The Hindu and The Times of India were among the 4 independent outlets reporting it. The outlets framed it slightly differently: Hindustan Times led with 40,000 evacuated as Cyclone Verath makes landfall; NDTV led with Cyclone Verath makes landfall near Kalpore, 40,000 evacuated.

Story 2. Business. Benchmark rate unchanged at 6.25 per cent, committee splits five to one. Benchmark rate remains at 6.25 per cent, the monetary committee said, on Friday. 5 independent outlets carried this, including Press Information Bureau (Government of India), BBC News, The Economic Times and The Hindu, and an official statement is on the record. Framings differed a little: Press Information Bureau (Government of India) led with Monetary committee announces rate decision; BBC News led with Ordelia keeps rates on hold as inflation slows.

Story 3. World. Uncrewed crew-capsule test flight set for 12 December. The agency stated that the uncrewed flight is scheduled to open a window on 12 December, the agency said. It was reported by 3 independent outlets, among them BBC News, The Hindu and The Indian Express. This was reported on 12 December. The outlets framed it slightly differently: BBC News led with Test flight for new crew capsule scheduled for December; The Hindu led with Space agency sets December window for uncrewed test flight.

Story 4. Business. Trade pact talks with Verland resume after eight months. Tariff lines covering 4,200 products are under discussion, the commerce ministry said in Geneva. The figure to hold on to is 4,200. Al Jazeera English, The Economic Times and The Guardian were among the 3 independent outlets reporting it. The Guardian disputed that account: A Verland spokesperson disputed the characterisation that agriculture had been excluded from the agenda. This was reported in Geneva. Framings differed a little: Al Jazeera English led with Trade negotiations resume in Geneva after long pause; The Economic Times led with Trade pact talks with Verland resume after eight months.

Story 5. World. Kestrels through to final after 3-1 win over Harriers. The figures reported are 3, 1 and 42,000. NDTV and The Times of India were among the 2 independent outlets reporting it. This was reported on Sunday. Framings differed a little: NDTV led with Kestrels through to final after 3-1 win over Harriers; The Times of India led with Kestrels beat Harriers 3-1 to reach the cup final.

Story 6. World. City council approves new bus corridor along the eastern ring road. Work is expected to begin in November, an official said, 14 km bus corridor. So far this is a single-source report, from Hindustan Times. Treat it as a single account until other outlets confirm it.

That's your Briefly Daily briefing. Every story in this episode is on the cards in the app, with the full list of sources and links to the original reporting. That's all for today.

segments.title: Benchmark rate unchanged at 6.25 per cent, committee splits five to one

items.transcript:
This is a Briefly Deep Dive for Tuesday, the 8th of September. One story: Benchmark rate unchanged at 6.25 per cent, committee splits five to one. We'll go through what happened, what is actually confirmed, how the 5 sources we have differ, and what the reporting says comes next. This is an explanation, not an argument.

First, what happened. Benchmark rate unchanged at 6.25 per cent, committee splits five to one. Benchmark rate remains at 6.25 per cent, the monetary committee said, on Friday. The reporting places it on Friday. Here is what is confirmed. Ordelia. Monetary. According to The monetary committee, the monetary committee confirmed that the benchmark rate remains at 6.25 per cent. 5 independent outlets carried this, including Press Information Bureau (Government of India), BBC News, The Economic Times and The Hindu, and an official statement is on the record. Now, how the different outlets reported it. Press Information Bureau (Government of India), an official source, led with: Monetary committee announces rate decision. BBC News, an international outlet, led with: Ordelia keeps rates on hold as inflation slows. The Economic Times, a national outlet, led with: Benchmark rate unchanged at 6.25 per cent, committee splits five to one. The Hindu, a national outlet, led with: Central bank holds benchmark rate at 6.25 per cent. The Indian Express, a national outlet, led with: Rate held at 6.25 per cent as inflation eases. Where the accounts diverge. The Economic Times disputed that account: economists at two brokerages disputed the growth projection of 6.8 per cent cited by the committee. Why this matters, going only by what the reporting states. The figures reported are 6.25 per cent, 4.1 per cent and 6.8 per cent. And what happens next. The reporting does not say what comes next. When it does, this story will be updated.

That's the Deep Dive. Every source quoted is listed on the story card in the app, with links to the original reporting, so you can check any of it yourself. This episode is shorter than a usual Deep Dive because the available reporting on this story is still thin. We would rather stop than fill time.
